name: Granite State Plastics
old_description: GSP is a full-service injection molder dedicated to our customer’s business growth through advanced production techniques, value-added service, and cost-effective innovations.
about:
Granite State Plastics operates from a 50,000-square-foot facility in Hudson, New Hampshire. Founded in 1969, the privately held company has built its reputation on continuous improvement, reinvestment in people and equipment, and cost-effective innovations for customer growth.

The company provides full-service injection molding, assembly, plastics engineering, tooling, and automation. Its Hudson plant houses 31 injection molding machines ranging from 40 to 450 tons, including Class 7 and Class 8 cleanroom capacity. Metrology capabilities include CMM with visual and touch probes, optical comparators, and custom gages.

Granite State Plastics serves the automotive, medical, and military sectors, delivering tight-tolerance components and managed tool-transfer programs for onshoring or supply-chain localization.

The company emphasizes technical capability, responsive supplier relationships, and a quality system built on APQP, FAI, IQ/OQ/PQ, and PPAP processes, underpinned by ISO 13485:2016 registration, UL recognition, and cGMP practices.

Great Blue Heron Furniture operates from Manchaca, Texas, where it was founded in 1991. The company remains privately held, though ownership details are not publicly disclosed. It began as a maker of western and contemporary western furniture, focusing on custom leather pieces.

The shop produces custom leather furniture, including sofas, chairs, ottomans, dining tables, and hand-carved wood pieces. Its product line spans armchairs, loveseats, sectionals, recliners, and specialty items such as hacienda tables and trophy-room furnishings. Current lead time for upholstery runs seven to nine weeks. The company does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Great Blue Heron serves residential clients and interior designers seeking high-end western-style furnishings. Project galleries reference installations such as the Croell Estate, Bailey Trophy Room, and various private ranch homes. The company also works with commercial hospitality projects, though specific industry sectors are not enumerated.

The company states its goal is to set the standard in quality and design for western and contemporary western furniture, offering products that are truly unique. A made-for-you custom design service guides clients from vision to finished piece, whether for a single statement chair or a fully furnished home.

name: Great Divide Fabrication LLC
old_description: Great Divide Services is here to serve all of your heating, venting,
about:
Great Divide Fabrication LLC operates as Great Divide Services in Buffalo, Wyoming. The business traces its roots to 2011 in company records, though founder Erik Burden states he launched the service operation in 2018 after progressing from apprentice to journeyman and manager. Burden, a master mechanical technician, owns and leads the company with his wife Jenn and their two sons living locally.

The shop provides heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning services for homes and businesses, including furnace and heat-pump installation, ductless mini-split systems, rooftop units, and 24-hour emergency repair. In addition to HVAC work, the team runs a custom sheet-metal fabrication operation, producing decorative tin work and fabricated metal components on a per-project basis. They also sell metal, piping, and miscellaneous supplies directly to walk-in customers. The fabrication side quotes per job after an on-site appointment, with rates varying by complexity.

Primary customers are residential and commercial property owners in Buffalo and the surrounding Johnson County area. The company services both new-construction and retrofit projects, handling everything from garage infrared heaters to commercial package units.

Burden emphasizes that a collaborative work environment and a commitment to craftsmanship set the operation apart. He cites his 15-plus years in the trade and a hands-on management style as the foundation for the company's focus on customer care and quality workmanship.

name: Great Plains Energy Corridor
old_description: The Corridor was tasked with providing innovative approaches that bring people together to advance the development of North Dakota's abundant and diverse energy resources.
about:
The Great Plains Energy Corridor was established in 2008 at Bismarck State College in Bismarck, North Dakota, through the initiative of former U.S. Senator Byron Dorgan. Operating as a division of the public two-year college, the Corridor was tasked with developing innovative approaches to bring stakeholders together for the advancement of North Dakota's diverse energy resources.

The organization does not manufacture products but instead provides information, education, outreach programs, and special events covering topics such as enhanced geothermal systems, renewable fuels, sustainable development, and energy transmission and storage technologies. It leverages Bismarck State College's nationally recognized energy education programs, which deliver state-of-the-art training to current and future industry employees. The Corridor's office is housed in the National Energy Center of Excellence (NECE) building on the BSC campus, a facility dedicated in September 2008 that incorporates a ground-source geothermal heat pump system, LEED-compliant lighting, a total energy heat recovery system, and Flexcrete—a construction material made with fly ash from coal combustion.

The Corridor serves partners across government, education, and the private sector, facilitating collaboration to promote energy-related activities through federal funding and other sources. Its audience includes energy industry professionals, students, policymakers, and researchers interested in North Dakota's energy landscape. The annual EmPowerND Energy Conference and the North Dakota Energy Report are among its key outreach vehicles, though the 2023 conference was canceled.

The Corridor's distinguishing feature is its integration within a college that operates a LEED-certified, energy-efficient facility purpose-built for energy education, giving it direct access to training infrastructure and a mandate to connect diverse energy stakeholders across the state.

name: Green Bay Plastics
old_description: – Custom manufacturer of plastic bottles, jars, and industrial components and products.
about:
Green Bay Plastics, Inc. has operated from Green Bay, Wisconsin since its incorporation in 1957. Originally part of Mosinee Paper Corporation, the company was bought out in 1989 by J. Kevin Hogan and his wife JoAnn, and remains family-owned today. Michael Hogan serves as president and general manager, with Patrick Hogan as vice president and Kathleen Hogan-Lesatz as controller and secretary-treasurer.

The company specializes in custom blow molding, producing plastic bottles, jars, handled containers, and industrial components. It designs and builds its own tooling, machinery, and auxiliary equipment in-house, and offers secondary services including labeling, painting, and custom packaging. Production runs range from a few thousand units to mass-production volumes.

Green Bay Plastics serves a diverse set of industries: food and beverage, lubricants, toy components, industrial applications, medical and healthcare packaging, dietary supplements, personal care, household products, sporting goods, and appliance parts such as fluid reservoirs for dishwashers and washing machines. Its customers are primarily wholesale distributors.

The firm emphasizes self-sufficiency through proprietary equipment design and a family-owned structure that has persisted since 1957, positioning it to control quality and lead times on custom blow-molded parts.

name: Green Brook Electronics
old_description: Large store, huge inventory, rentals, repairs, books, records, surplus and more!
about:
Green Brook Electronics was founded in 1974 in Green Brook, New Jersey, and has operated as a privately held supplier of electronic components and instrumentation. In 2018 the company relocated to a larger facility in North Plainfield, New Jersey, expanding its footprint to over seven times the size of its original store.

The business stocks more than 300,000 distinct line items across multiple warehouse locations, ranging from semiconductors, relays, capacitors, and resistors to wire, cable, fuses, and audio/video cables. Beyond distribution, Green Brook Electronics operates a retail storefront, an equipment rental center, a repair shop capable of board-level and surface-mount work, a movie-prop rental division featuring vintage test equipment and computers, a technology studio offering soldering and Arduino classes, a vinyl record center, and a component-identification service.

Customers include large technology firms, industrial buyers, medical-equipment operators, film-production companies, hobbyists, and the general public. The company ships worldwide and emphasizes its ability to source obsolete and long-lead-time parts.

Green Brook Electronics distinguishes itself through its deep inventory of hard-to-find components, its repair expertise across consumer and industrial electronics, and its eclectic mix of retail, rental, and educational services that serve both professional engineers and enthusiasts.

name: Green Mountain Furniture
old_description: We trust that upon completing your virtual tour, you will accept our invitation to come and see for yourself why we have been singing since 1975, “Green Mountain Furniture, more than meets the eye."
about:
Green Mountain Furniture has operated in Ossipee, New Hampshire, since 1975. The store takes its name from the mountain range that rises behind the property, and its 40,000-square-foot showroom spans multiple floors in a building noted for its creaking wood floors and a layout that changes regularly.

The business functions as a full-line home furnishings retailer. Its showroom carries living-room, bedroom, dining, home-office, and kitchen furniture, along with mattresses, adjustable bases, area rugs, lighting, window treatments, bath décor, and decorative accessories. Brands represented include Craftmaster, Flexsteel, and Best Home. A delivery service is offered with an optional removal of old pieces.

The customer base is residential shoppers furnishing primary homes, vacation cabins, and lodges. The product mix spans upholstered collections (sofas, sectionals, recliners, sleeper sofas), wood case goods, bedding, and accent pieces. Shoppers can browse in person or request product dimensions and SKU listings for specific collections such as Craftmaster’s SS, F9, M9, C9, and L9 series or Flexsteel’s Thornton and Catalina groups.

The company positions itself on an experience-first model: sales staff are not commissioned, the showroom encourages hands-on testing — sitting, reclining, lying on beds — and two warranty programs are highlighted, a Guardsman five-year fabric and leather protection plan and a 100-night sleep guarantee on mattresses.

name: Greg Moser & Engineering Inc
old_description: Moser has been leading the competition since 1986 and continues to provide industry leading products. We pride ourselves in our ability to supply quality America-made products, at an affordable price
about:
Moser Engineering operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Portland, Indiana. The company was founded in 1986 by Greg Moser, who initially launched the business to support his own drag-racing habit at the Muncie strip. Today it remains family owned and operated.

The shop forges, heat-treats, and machines U.S. steel sourced from domestic mills to produce custom axles, complete rear-end assemblies, differential options, brake packages, and chassis/suspension components. Product lines include the Muscle Pak rear assemblies, circle-track/oval packages, and applications for GM, Ford, and Mopar platforms. Most custom orders ship in two business days or less.

Customers range from professional drag and circle-track teams to street-rod builders, Jeep and truck owners, and project-car restorers. The company's own race team campaigns two rigs and multiple cars, putting new components through on-track validation before release.

Moser Engineering cites three pillars for its approach: domestic manufacturing with full process control, rapid turnaround enabled by that control, and direct racing experience that informs product development. Staff includes current and former racers and builders, many with decades of tenure.

name: Grillo & Co
old_description: Grillo and Co creates beautiful bespoke furniture for your home or workplace. Operating almost entirely by commission, we custom design and hand make each piece to your exact specifications at our workshop in Golden, Colorado. We will help you visualize your ideas and, once you’re completely happy with the proposed design, we hand-craft your unique heirloom piece of furniture.
about:
Grillo & Co operates a woodworking workshop in Golden, Colorado, where founder John Grillo produces custom furniture on commission. Grillo trained at the Thomas Chippendale International School of Furniture in Scotland, where his work earned the Richard Demarco Prize and recognition in Furniture & Cabinetmaking Magazine and The Scottish Times. A member of the Fine Furniture Guild, he established the studio to blend contemporary and traditional techniques in one-off pieces for homes and workplaces.

The shop designs and hand-builds freestanding furniture including dining tables, writing desks, console tables, side tables, and cabinets. Each project begins with a client consultation and 3D sketches, followed by a 50% deposit and fabrication using joinery such as dovetails, tambour doors, and parquetry. Materials range from domestic hardwoods — walnut, maple, cherry, figured cherry — to exotic veneers like pepperwood and burl walnut. Production is low-volume, single-piece flow with no stated facility size or headcount beyond the owner.

Grillo & Co serves residential and commercial clients seeking heirloom-quality pieces. Past commissions include a walnut coffee table for a homeowner, multiple pieces for a repeat collector, and unusual custom projects for a client who returned for a second order. The company also offers home and office visits to match existing décor, indicating an interior-design adjacent clientele.

The firm emphasizes award-winning craftsmanship, direct designer-to-client pricing, and freedom from commercial supply-chain delays. Grillo’s Chippendale training and guild membership underpin a design philosophy that treats furniture as functional art, with every detail — down to dovetail style — tailored to the buyer.

The process emphasizes artisanal methods rather than mass production, though details on facility size, headcount, or annual volume are not publicly specified. The company's online presence includes a gallery and tools to explore fabrics by color and pattern.

The fabrics are designed for drapery, upholstery, and wall-covering applications, serving interior designers, decorators, and homeowners seeking custom textile solutions. The company's gallery and online color and pattern explorers indicate a focus on aesthetic customization for residential and commercial projects.

Groves Bros. distinguishes itself through its commitment to handcrafted individuality and Venetian-inspired craftsmanship, positioning its products as timeless, one-of-a-kind textiles made domestically in Texas.
